name: Cross-Channel Correlation Analysis
description: Analyzes inter-channel correlation patterns — real camera pipelines introduce characteristic cross-channel correlations absent in AI generation.
mechanism:
This method exploits the inter-channel dependencies introduced by the camera imaging pipeline to distinguish real photographs from AI-generated images:

1. **Color Channel Decomposition**: The image is decomposed into R, G, and B channels (or converted to YCbCr/Lab space). For each pair of channels, the Pearson correlation coefficient is computed on overlapping 8×8 blocks, producing a spatial correlation map.

2. **Pipeline Correlation Fingerprint**: Real cameras introduce specific cross-channel correlations through CFA demosaicing, white-balance gain multiplication, and color matrix transformations. These create structured dependencies: e.g., the G–R correlation pattern follows the Bayer CFA layout with a period of 2 pixels. The method extracts the 2D autocorrelation of the inter-channel correlation map to detect these periodic signatures.

3. **GAN/Diffusion Artifact Detection**: AI generators produce each channel independently or through learned convolutions that lack hardware pipeline correlations. The method measures the Frobenius norm of the difference between the observed cross-channel correlation matrix and the expected correlation matrix from known camera models.

4. **Block-Level Inconsistency**: For tampered images, the cross-channel correlation structure varies between authentic and manipulated regions. A sliding-window analysis (32×32 blocks, stride 8) computes local correlation deviations, flagging blocks where the correlation pattern breaks from the dominant camera signature.
parameters:
Block size: 8×8 pixels for correlation computation
Sliding window: 32×32 with stride 8 for local analysis
Color spaces: RGB, YCbCr, and CIE Lab
Correlation threshold: 0.15 deviation from expected model
Minimum image size: 256×256 pixels
accuracy: 78–88% detection accuracy on real vs. AI-generated images. Performance improves to 91% when combined with CFA pattern analysis. False positive rate of 6–9% on heavily post-processed authentic photos.
source: Chierchia, G., Cozzolino, D., Poggi, G., Sansone, C., & Verdoliva, L. (2014). PRNU-based forgery detection with regularity constraints and global optimization. IEEE International Workshop on Multimedia Signal Processing.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated images that lack realistic inter-channel dependencies. Identifying spliced regions where the cross-channel correlation structure differs from the host image. Verifying camera authenticity by matching correlation patterns to known sensor models.
strengths:
• Exploits fundamental camera pipeline physics that AI generators cannot easily replicate
• Effective across different GAN architectures (StyleGAN, ProGAN, BigGAN)
• Provides spatial localization of tampered regions through block-level analysis
• Robust to JPEG compression up to quality factor 70
• Complements CFA and PRNU-based detection methods
limitations:
• Performance degrades significantly after heavy color grading or HDR tone mapping
• Requires minimum resolution of 256×256 for reliable correlation estimation
• May produce false positives on images shot with non-standard color pipelines (e.g., Foveon sensors)
• Latest diffusion models (SDXL, DALL-E 3) can partially mimic channel correlations
